note: Thresholds set by engineering judgment (t4g.micro sizing, 3-instance min ASG, known low traffic). Live-fire verified 2026-09-02: all 3 alarms manually forced to ALARM via aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state, real SNS email delivery confirmed on each.

alerts.name: ce-capstone-bouncer-dev-high-5xx-rate
alerts.description: Combined target + ELB 5xx responses exceeded 5 in a 5-minute window
alerts.reasoning: Raw count, not percentage -- low traffic volume makes percentage noisy (1 request = 100%).

alerts.name: ce-capstone-bouncer-dev-unhealthy-hosts
alerts.description: At least 1 target group host unhealthy for 2 consecutive minutes
alerts.reasoning: Any unhealthy host matters on a 3-instance minimum ASG; 2 periods avoids alerting on a transient blip mid-deploy.

alerts.name: ce-capstone-bouncer-dev-rds-high-cpu
alerts.description: RDS CPU utilization above 80% for 10 consecutive minutes
alerts.reasoning: db.t4g.micro is burstable; sustained high CPU over two periods means burst credits are being spent down, not a brief spike.
